text: DEWA has built the tools. But technology deployed is not the same as value realised. That gap — between access and adoption — is where this programme begins. And this brief sets out exactly how to close it.
One-point-five million tickets. Eighty percent are avoidable navigation questions. Employees add further demand across enterprise apps. The friction is measurable — and DEWA is already paying.

SAP WalkMe places an Action Bar inside every application DEWA uses. As employees work, Joule skills surface. Guided steps appear. Tasks complete — without switching apps. More work done right the first time.
Today RAMMAS answers — and stops. With WalkMe, each answer becomes a guided journey: activation, reconnection, billing — from question to done. Savings: one million dollars estimated.
Eight value streams. Fewer tickets. Less custom code. Faster onboarding. Lower support demand. Easier change. Less rework. RAMMAS replaced. One programme delivering measurable value.

Twenty-six million estimated over five years. Five million invested. Net positive from year one. A five-to-one return — before optimisation has even begun. These are planning estimates DEWA can validate and improve.
Delay has a price. Tickets undeflected. Escalations ongoing. Technical debt growing. DEWA's AI capability — at risk of going undiscovered. Doing nothing is not a zero-cost option.

Start with security and baselines. Use the first hundred days to prove the highest-impact services. Then scale from one thousand to three thousand employees — phase by phase, on evidence. The roadmap is clear.
The recommendation: proceed. Phased, measurable, evidence-based. One programme — connecting DEWA's digital investments to the moment of work.
